function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—instead it was gradually understood through contributions from many scientists over several millennia:

| Era | Key Contributors | What they did |
|-----|------------------|---------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | *Thales of Miletus* (~600 BCE) | Noted static charge when rubbing amber (“electrum”). |
| **17th–18th Century** | *William Gilbert* (1544‑1603) | Coined the term *electricus*, studied magnetism vs. electrostatics. |
| | *Benjamin Franklin* (1706‑1790) | Demonstrated lightning as electrical discharge; introduced positive/negative charges. |
| | *Alessandro Volta* (1745‑1827) | Invented the voltaic pile—first chemical battery, proving continuous electric flow. |
| | *Luigi Galvani* & *André-Marie Ampère* | Explored bioelectric phenomena and formulated laws of electromagnetism. |
| **19th Century** | *Michael Faraday* (1791‑1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction; laid groundwork for generators and motors. |
| | *James Clerk Maxwell* (1831‑1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into four equations describing fields. |

So while there isn’t a single discoverer, the cumulative work of thinkers such as Thales, Gilbert, Franklin, Volta, Galvani, Ampère, Faraday, and Maxwell turned scattered observations into modern physics and engineering.
